findings.title: Military personnel data exposed in breach, agency warns
findings.summary_md: Military Times reported on Sept. 24, 2026, that a vulnerability in a Defense Manpower Data Center file-sharing system allowed unauthorized users to access unencrypted files between October 2025 and July 16, 2026. A notification letter confirmed exposed data included Social Security numbers, names, dates of birth, contact information, sex, race, and military occupational specialty. The article notes DMDC discovered the issue July 16 and patched it, and that approximately four million DoD personnel may be affected according to two people familiar with the incident.

findings.title: Pentagon breach exposed sensitive data on nearly 3 million people
findings.summary_md: ABC News reported on Sept. 28, 2026, that a Pentagon personnel database breach exposed sensitive information on 2.76 million living people and 294,000 deceased individuals. The breach involved unauthorized access between October 2025 and July 2026 through a file-sharing system vulnerability. The article notes Military Times first reported the breach last week, and confirms no evidence of misuse as of publication.

findings.title: More than 3 million people affected by military data breach
findings.summary_md: Federal News Network reported on Sept. 28, 2026, that a DMDC information system breach exposed unencrypted records of nearly 2.8 million living and 294,000 deceased individuals. The unauthorized access spanned October 2025 to July 2026, stemming from a file-sharing vulnerability discovered July 16. The Pentagon said there is no indication of misuse and is offering 12 months of credit monitoring through IDX.
